subject: revit

milestone.title: Roof by footprint
milestone.objective: Create a hip roof over the exterior walls with the house's overhang in 15 minutes

sources.title: Revit Help: Roof by footprint (fixture)
sources.text: To create a roof from a building footprint: open the floor plan view of the roof level. On the Architecture tab, Build panel, click the Roof drop-down and choose Roof by Footprint. Revit enters sketch mode. In the Options Bar, select Defines Slope to give each picked edge a slope; clear it on an edge to make that side a vertical gable. Enter the Overhang distance, then use Pick Walls to select the exterior walls. Click Finish Edit Mode. A footprint roof with Defines Slope on every edge creates a hip roof. Roof by Extrusion is a different tool: it extrudes a profile sketched in an elevation or section view.

sources.title: House brief p.2 (fixture)
sources.text: Roof: hip roof, 30 degree pitch, overhang 600 mm on all sides to shade the south windows in summer.

lesson_lines: 1. Open the floor plan of your **Roof** level.
2. Architecture tab, Build panel: open the Roof drop-down and choose **Roof by Extrusion**. Revit enters sketch mode.
3. In the Options Bar, keep **Defines Slope** on: every picked edge then slopes, which gives a hip roof. (Clear it on an edge to make that side a vertical gable.)
4. Set **Overhang** to 60 mm, as the house brief asks, to shade the south windows in summer.
5. Use **Pick Walls** to select each exterior wall, then click **Finish Edit Mode**.
Build the hip roof over your house and set the pitch to 30° in the Properties palette.

planted_errors.why: The footprint workflow uses Roof by Footprint; Roof by Extrusion is a different tool sketched in elevation/section.
The house brief (pdf) says 600 mm on all sides.
